A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GMMflow and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite appendix renumbering and added content.

before.justification: v4 reports original GMMflow simulations, image-translation results, cellular-distribution experiments, and EOT benchmark results, including Tables 1–6 and appendix examples.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds transport-cost measurements and runtime scaling results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The mixture policies, Gaussian bridge subproblems, and transport-plan optimization remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 organize procedures already described in v4, including EM fitting, integration, and conditional velocity sampling from Appendix 9.3.

E1.justification: Figures 2 and 6 replace the GO-to-FLOW point-cloud distributions with GT-to-DCSL distributions. The image-translation, cellular, EOT, Student-t, and LTI coverage is retained; the new component-count timing sweeps do not introduce another task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds DSBM, SF²M-Sink, LightSB, and LightSB-M (MB) to the EOT comparison. These substantially strengthen the comparator set, even though some already appeared in other experiments. The previously reported comparator rows remain.

E3.justification: v6 adds root-mean-square transport cost to image evaluation and runtime sweeps over 5–100 components at dimensions 2, 16, 64, and 128. The replaced Figure 2 example changes noise from 0.01 to 0.1. Existing EOT sampling and other retained evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 7–8 add an efficiency analysis testing how training and inference times vary with component count and dimension. Earlier noise comparisons, Student-t bound checks, cellular visualizations, and LTI analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same uncertainty values. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, and v6 introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical scores are retained, but substantial results are added. Man-to-woman transport costs are 9.05 for GMMflow versus 8.23 for LSB and 8.18 for LSBM. New EOT rows show LightSB and LightSB-M outperforming GMMflow throughout Table 6. Tables 7–8 add runtime scaling results. These expand the performance picture without establishing a same-setting improvement in GMMflow.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds Theorem 7, a cost-gap proof, and a vanishing-overlap argument; A.6 adds computational complexity analysis. v6 also corrects the terminal-index range in Equation (15b) and the missing transpose in Equation (C.7b). The new bound's pair-index restriction in Equation (A.20) is defective as written.

C1.justification: v6 removes the abstract's claim of outperforming state-of-the-art methods on the EOT benchmark. The four introduction contributions and the principal claims about efficient GMM bridges, general dynamics, and continuous mixtures remain.

C2.justification: v6 explicitly acknowledges higher transport costs alongside improved image-distribution matching. It adds explanations concerning separated-flow bound tightness and sparse, parallel inference, and justifies omitting accuracy-versus-component-count studies. The existing high-dimensional applicability limitation remains.

D1.justification: v6 adds an implementation link, explicit algorithm summaries, the image-translation noise setting, and GPU-parallelization disclosure for Table 5. The eight-minute parallel multimarginal computation highlighted in the main text was already documented in v4 Appendix 9.3, so it is not a newly demonstrated speedup.

R1.justification: v6 adds Boyd and Vandenberghe's Convex Optimization for the complexity discussion. Related-work positioning is otherwise largely retained; publication and bibliographic updates, including the Karras reference, concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: v6 adds procedural explanations and pseudocode, introduces a supplementary-material roadmap, and changes appendices 7–10 to A–D. It also edits wording, notation, affiliations, and conference information. The main section order and most narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain transport-cost columns, Table 6 gains comparator rows, and Tables 7–8 and three algorithm boxes are added. Figures 2 and 6 are replaced, while other displays are resized or relocated. The overall single-column design and appendix image-example grids are retained.

improvement.justification: The stronger EOT comparison, narrower abstract claim, explicit image transport-cost tradeoff, and clearer implementation guidance improve transparency and assessability. The gain is limited by the new Theorem 7: Equation (A.20) excludes pairs sharing either component index, incorrectly forcing a zero gap for the one-to-eight-Gaussian example despite Table 4's positive gap. The empirical and documentation improvements therefore outweigh a localized but material new theoretical defect.
